WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Fox’s Spot the Difference Worksheet for Age 4

Two picnic pictures, five sneaky changes — find the hat, the butterfly, the snack, the apple and one secret mushroom spot.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Spot-the-difference trains visual discrimination — the eye-for-detail that later tells b from d on a page. Every change is a colour or object swap a four-year-old can truly find, and comparing the pictures aloud (“in this one the hat is…?”) turns searching into language.

  • Visual discrimination
  • Comparing two pictures
  • Colour and object comparison
  • Careful looking

On the sheet: Find and circle 5 differences!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Robot’s Rainbow Logic Worksheet for Age 4

Red, blue, red, blue… finish three of Robot’s picture patterns by circling what comes next.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Pattern completion is prediction practice: the eye hears the rhythm, and the answer follows from the rule rather than a guess. Three different pattern types (color, shape, size) keep the rule-hunting honest — each row must be read fresh.

  • Finishing ABAB patterns
  • Size patterns (small/big)
  • Checking the rule before answering
  • Circle with control

On the sheet: Circle what comes next!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Lion’s Shadow Safari Worksheet for Age 4

A giraffe, an elephant, a crocodile — draw lines matching every safari animal to its shadow.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Shadow matching is silhouette geometry: the outline carries all the information, so your child must attend to necks, trunks and snouts rather than colors. Say the tell-tale feature out loud before each line is drawn — “the long neck goes to the long neck!”

  • Silhouette matching
  • Feature spotting (neck, trunk, snout)
  • Line drawing
  • Safari animal vocabulary

On the sheet: Match each animal to its shadow!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Squirrel’s Acorn Maze Worksheet for Age 4

Help Squirrel reach the golden acorn — trace a real path through the maze without crossing the walls.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Maze tracing builds planning ahead: eyes scout the route, the pencil follows, and dead ends teach backtracking without tears. The maze sheet doubles as pencil-control practice — slow, steady lines between the walls are exactly the skill early writing wants.

  • Maze planning and tracing
  • Pencil control
  • Backtracking from dead ends
  • Start-to-finish persistence

On the sheet: Help Squirrel find the golden acorn!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Bear’s Big-to-Small Parade Worksheet for Age 4

Four bears, one parade — write 1, 2, 3 and 4 from biggest to smallest so the march can begin.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Ordering a whole set by size is harder than comparing two objects: each round asks “which is the biggest one LEFT?” The parade story keeps it playful, and the leader bear (who wears the hat) is deliberately not in the race — a nice first exclusion rule.

  • Ordering 4 objects by size
  • Biggest-to-smallest language
  • Number writing 1–4
  • Comparing across a set

On the sheet: Write 1, 2, 3, and 4 from biggest to smallest!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Owl’s Memory Magic Worksheet for Age 4

Apple, star, car, leaf, cupcake — one item vanished from the copied panel. Circle what is missing!

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Spot-the-missing-item is memory made visible: hold the first panel in your head, scan the copy, and name the gap. The blue toy car’s empty dashed outline gives a strong hint for beginners — cover the left panel for the expert version.

  • Visual memory
  • Comparing two panels
  • Naming missing items
  • Careful scanning

On the sheet: Look carefully. Circle what is missing!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Bunny’s Puzzle Blocks Worksheet for Age 4

A color grid, a star-heart pattern, a growing tower — circle the block that completes each puzzle.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Three puzzles, three different completion rules: all-four-colors-different, an ABAB shape pattern, and a tower that shrinks as it grows. Naming the rule out loud before circling is the whole lesson — rules are things you can say.

  • Completing a color grid
  • ABAB shape patterns
  • Size-ordered towers
  • Stating the rule

On the sheet: Circle the block that completes each puzzle!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Dinosaur Egg Detective Worksheet for Age 4

Five eggs match, one does not — circle the odd egg in each row: red among blue, dots among zigzags, one giant egg.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Odd-one-out across a whole set sharpens the comparing eye: color first, then pattern, then size. The printed sheet always hides the odd egg last in its row, so play the online game too — it deals the eggs in mixed order so the detective work stays honest.

  • Odd-one-out by color, pattern and size
  • Comparing across a set
  • Explaining the difference
  • Careful circling

On the sheet: Find the egg that does not belong!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Penguin’s Ice Path Worksheet for Age 4

Circle, triangle, square — hop the ice floes in the key’s order and lead Penguin to the fish.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Following a key is multi-step instruction following: the top strip gives the order, the floes test it, and the decoys punish pattern-reading too fast. Say the key aloud like a chant — “circle, triangle, square!” — then tap or circle the path.

  • Following a picture key
  • Ordered sequences
  • Ignoring decoys
  • Ice and shape vocabulary

On the sheet: Follow the shapes to reach the fish!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Monkey’s Odd-One-Out Market Worksheet for Age 4

Three apples and a banana — at Monkey’s market, circle the picture that is different in every box.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Market-stall odd-one-outs pair food and toy vocabulary with the comparing eye. The printed sheet always puts the odd item third, so after circling, play the online game — it shuffles the stalls and keeps the skill, not the position, sharp.

  • Odd-one-out spotting
  • Food and toy vocabulary
  • Explaining what is different
  • Circle with control

On the sheet: Circle the picture that is different!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Elephant’s Size Sorting Circus Worksheet for Age 4

A mouse, a dog, an elephant — draw lines matching every circus friend to the right-sized tent.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Size matching across three scales: the tent must FIT the animal, which asks your child to imagine the mouse inside the big tent and giggle at the elephant in the small one. Fit-and-mismatch reasoning is early measurement thinking.

  • Size matching (small/medium/large)
  • Fit reasoning
  • Circus vocabulary
  • Line drawing

On the sheet: Match each animal to the right-sized tent!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Owl’s Secret Code Worksheet for Age 4

Red star = 1, blue heart = 2, yellow sun = 3 — crack Owl’s picture code and finish every row.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A picture code is a symbol system: this shape STANDS FOR that number. Decoding three rows builds the idea that marks carry meaning — the exact insight reading runs on. Read the key aloud together, then let your child be the code-breaker.

  • Symbol substitution
  • Number recognition 1–3
  • Following a key
  • Early code thinking

On the sheet: Use the picture code to finish each row!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Panda’s Missing Puzzle Worksheet for Age 4

A wing, a roof, a wheel — circle the piece that completes each of Panda’s pictures.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Missing-piece puzzles ask what a picture NEEDS rather than what it shows: a butterfly without a wing cannot fly, a house without a roof lets the rain in. Function reasoning (what does this piece do?) is the comprehension behind the circling.

  • Missing-piece reasoning
  • Function thinking (wings fly, roofs shelter)
  • Object vocabulary
  • Circle with control

On the sheet: Circle the piece that completes each picture!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Raccoon’s Clue Hunt Worksheet for Age 4

A wheel, handlebars, a bell — read Raccoon’s clues and circle the object they describe.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Clue-to-object inference adds parts up to a whole: three clues, one answer, two near-misses. Say each clue aloud and wonder together before circling — “what has ALL of those?” — and the last clue row (a face, hands, numbers) lands as a delightful aha.

  • Clue-to-object inference
  • Parts-of-a-whole reasoning
  • Object vocabulary
  • Explaining an answer

On the sheet: Look at the clues. Circle the right object!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Dragon’s Treasure Logic Worksheet for Age 4

A splash and a shape — follow BOTH clues to the one treasure chest that matches each time.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Two-clue logic is real deduction: color AND shape must both fit, so each wrong chest can be rejected out loud (“right color, wrong shape!”). The printed sheet lands every answer on chest B — the online game shuffles the chests so the clues, not the middle spot, get read.

  • Two-clue deduction
  • Color and shape testing
  • Rejecting near-misses
  • Treasure vocabulary

On the sheet: Follow the clues. Circle the correct treasure chest!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Turtle’s Bridge Builder Worksheet for Age 4

Square, circle, square… circle the shape that fills the gap in each of Turtle’s bridges.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Three bridges, three pattern rules: ABAB shapes, an AAB pattern with the circle as the beat, and a three-color cycle. Filling a GAP (rather than continuing a row) adds one more thinking step — the pattern must run backwards from the gap too.

  • Gap-filling in patterns
  • ABA and ABC cycles
  • Reading patterns both ways
  • Shape and color naming

On the sheet: Circle the shape that fills each gap!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Giraffe’s Tallest Tower Worksheet for Age 4

Three towers in every row — circle the tallest one so Giraffe can cheer.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Comparing heights across three towers blends counting with measuring: count the blocks, or eyeball the top edge. The rows are arranged so the tallest tower changes position each time — the answer must be found fresh, never remembered.

  • Height comparison
  • Counting blocks
  • Tallest/shortest language
  • Circle with control

On the sheet: Circle the tallest tower in each row!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Fox’s Logic Picnic Worksheet for Age 4

A puzzle piece AND a food name one basket each — match both clues to find Fox’s picnic baskets.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

This is two-clue deduction: neither clue alone picks the basket. The piece gives the colour, the food gives the contents, and each row offers one right-colour-wrong-food and one right-food-wrong-colour basket — so both clues must be used. Saying it aloud (“green… and an apple… so the green apple basket!”) is the whole skill.

  • Two-clue deduction
  • Colour and content matching
  • Rejecting near-misses
  • Explaining an answer

On the sheet: Use the clues to find the right picnic basket!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Koala’s Sorting Station Worksheet for Age 4

Six toys, three boxes — sort every toy by its SHAPE, even when the colors try to trick you.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The deliberate trick: a red triangle does NOT go in the red box — shapes sort, colors distract. Beating the color trap is a genuine logic milestone, and saying “triangle to the triangle box!” while sorting makes the rule stick.

  • Sorting by shape
  • Ignoring color distractors
  • Shape vocabulary
  • Cut-and-sort persistence

On the sheet: Match each toy to the right box!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Octopus’s Shell Mystery Worksheet for Age 4

Pink, blue, pink, blue… circle the shell that comes next in every one of Octopus’s patterns.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Shell patterns step up gently: a simple AB color pattern, an ABC size pattern (small, small, BIG), and an ABB shape pattern. Naming each rule in words (“two little ones, then the big one!”) is the language half of patterning.

  • AB, ABB and ABC patterns
  • Size and shape patterns
  • Stating pattern rules
  • Shell vocabulary

On the sheet: Circle the shell that comes next!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Unicorn’s Rainbow Route Worksheet for Age 4

Red, blue, yellow — hop the rainbow colors in the key’s order and lead the unicorn to the castle.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A color-key route adds order to color knowledge: red first, then blue, then yellow, with three off-key colors waiting to mislead. Chant the key like a song, then hop the circles — the castle at the end is the celebration.

  • Following a color key
  • Ordered sequences
  • Resisting off-key colors
  • Rainbow color naming

On the sheet: Follow the rainbow colors to the castle!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Hedgehog’s Odd Shape Garden Worksheet for Age 4

Four shapes match, one does not — circle the odd flower, the odd pot and the odd butterfly.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

This garden moves odd-one-out beyond color: the odd flower has pointed petals, the odd pot is round, the odd butterfly wears mixed shapes. Naming WHAT is different (not just which one) is the highest rung — ask for the why every time.

  • Odd-one-out by shape
  • Petals, pots and wings vocabulary
  • Explaining differences
  • Circle with control

On the sheet: Circle the shape that does not belong!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Bear’s Picnic Order Worksheet for Age 4

Basket, play, eat, wash — write 1, 2, 3 and 4 to show the right order for Bear’s picnic.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A four-beat picnic story with a built-in real routine: carrying the basket starts the day, washing the plate ends it. Sequencing familiar routines lets your child check the answer against life experience — the strongest comprehension check there is.

  • Sequencing a 4-step routine
  • Number writing 1–4
  • First/then/next/last words
  • Routine reasoning

On the sheet: Write 1, 2, 3, and 4 to show the right order!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Raccoon’s Secret Object Worksheet for Age 4

Color plus shape — follow both clues and circle Raccoon’s secret object in every row.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Two clues at once (blue AND round) is the earliest true deduction: each object gets tested against both clues, and near-misses get rejected with reasons. The near-misses are deliberate — a blue car fits one clue only — and rejecting them aloud is the lesson.

  • Two-clue deduction (color + shape)
  • Testing objects against clues
  • Size words (small, big)
  • Explaining rejections

On the sheet: Follow the clues. Circle the secret object!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Fox’s Gear Workshop Worksheet for Age 4

A round spot, a big gear-shaped spot, a missing colour — circle the gear that fits each of Fox’s machines.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Fitting gears into machines rehearses shape-and-size reasoning with a WHY worth saying: the round gear spins in a round spot, the big gear fills the big spot (a square cannot spin!), and the last machine simply needs its blue gear back. Each wrong piece has a reason, and reasons are the learning.

  • Shape and size matching
  • Fit reasoning (why it fits)
  • Colour matching
  • Explaining the why

On the sheet: Circle the gear that fits each machine!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Panda’s Balloon Logic Worksheet for Age 4

Blue + heart, small + green, red + triangle — follow both clues to Panda’s balloon in every group.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Balloon logic rehearses two-clue deduction with a party wrapper: pattern AND color must both fit. The four balloons per group make a tidy test grid, and the near-misses (blue star, red heart) are perfect for out-loud rejection practice.

  • Two-clue deduction (pattern + color)
  • Size words
  • Balloon and pattern vocabulary
  • Careful circling

On the sheet: Use the clues. Circle the correct balloon!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Dragon’s Crystal Challenge Worksheet for Age 4

Red, blue, red, blue… find the missing crystal in each of Dragon’s three patterns.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Crystal patterns climb the difficulty ladder: an AB color row, an AAB size row (small, small, BIG — wait for it), and an ABC shape row (triangle, square, circle, again). Each missing gem is found by saying the rule, then testing the choices against it.

  • AB, AAB and ABC patterns
  • Size sequences
  • Shape cycles
  • Crystal and gem vocabulary

On the sheet: Find the missing crystal in each pattern!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Penguin’s Ice Block Builder Worksheet for Age 4

Each ice tower misses its top block — circle the block that completes every tower.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Three towers, three completion rules, one shared block pile: blues that shrink as they stack, a red-yellow alternation, and shapes that take turns. The printed sheet shows one big pile, so read each tower’s rule aloud and let the pile be raided honestly.

  • Completing size, color and shape towers
  • Stating the rule
  • Matching pieces to gaps
  • Block vocabulary

On the sheet: Circle the block that completes each tower!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Bunny’s Path Detective Worksheet for Age 4

Red circle, yellow star, purple heart — hop Bunny’s path in the key’s order and find the carrot!

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A detective key with three shapes and three decoys: the chant goes circle-star-heart, and every off-key shape (squares, triangles, diamonds) answers with a giggle. Keys, order and self-control in one cheerful path — the carrot is the trophy.

  • Following a three-step key
  • Ordered hopping
  • Resisting decoy shapes
  • Shape and color naming

On the sheet: Follow the clues to find the carrot!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Logic Castle Graduation Worksheet for Age 4

Three final puzzles guard the castle: finish the pattern, spot the odd fruit, find the biggest teddy.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The graduation sheet mixes the class’s three core moves on one page: pattern completion (red-blue-red-blue), odd-one-out (banana among apples) and size comparison (the middle teddy is the big one). Finishing it earns the castle — and a very proud logic graduate.

  • Mixed logic skills (pattern, odd-one, size)
  • AB pattern completion
  • Odd-one-out spotting
  • Biggest comparison

On the sheet: Solve all three puzzles to finish the adventure!
